key_information_units.information: Novaturas Group reported consolidated revenues of EUR 201 million in 2024, representing a 3.6% decrease from EUR 208 million in 2023. The Group incurred an audited net loss of EUR 7.6 million (compared to a profit of EUR 3.4 million in 2023) with an adjusted EBITDA of EUR -449 thousand (versus EUR 5.2 million in 2023). Earnings per share amounted to EUR -0.97 in 2024.
key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword; Financial information section; Statements of comprehensive income; Note 27

key_information_units.information: Key period-over-period changes included an 8% decline in served travelers (239 thousand in 2024 vs 259 thousand in 2023) and a swing from positive to negative EBITDA (€5.2m to -€6.1m). The result was primarily driven by increased competitive pressures in the Baltic travel market, particularly in Turkey and Greek islands, coupled with a one-off EUR 5.7 million goodwill impairment related to the Estonian cash-generating unit.

In early 2025, strategic investor Neset Kockar acquired 23.2% of Novaturas' shares (completed on 30 April 2025), with a planned further acquisition to reach 33.19% by autumn 2025. Kockar, a Turkish tourism businessman, provided the Group with loan facilities totaling EUR 2 million post-reporting-period, and is expected to bring synergies in destinations popular with Baltic travelers, potentially expanding hotel and travel offerings.
key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword; Note 29 (Events after the reporting period)

key_information_units.information: Travel demand trends showed significant growth to Spain (149% increase in passengers to Malaga, Barcelona, and Mallorca compared to 2022) and an 8% rise in long-haul travel. Popular long-haul destinations included Vietnam (+367%), Phuket (+23%), and Zanzibar (+21%), with long-haul flights achieving a 98.9% load factor in Q4 2024.

Operational performance improved materially in Q4 2024, with adjusted EBITDA reaching EUR 2.3 million and a load factor of 98.9% (compared to 96.7% in Q4 2023). This improvement followed optimization of the travel program and better destination management, reducing the share of last-minute trips which negatively impact financial results.

Liquidity position weakened with cash and cash equivalents decreasing to EUR 394 thousand at 31 December 2024 from EUR 3,347 thousand in 2023. Borrowings increased to EUR 9,250 thousand (from EUR 8,682 thousand in 2023), and the Group did not comply with all financial covenants as of year-end, requiring waivers from lenders.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Statements of cash flows; Note 14; Liquidity management section

key_information_units.information: Segment performance was dominated by flight packages, which accounted for the majority of revenue but saw a 12.3% decline in passenger numbers compared to 2023. Other segments included sightseeing tours by coach (3.7 thousand passengers) and by air (2.1 thousand), with 'other sales' (flight tickets and hotel bookings) growing by 12.8%.
